questions.question: What is the difference between val and var?
questions.answer: A val is a read-only reference assigned once; a var can be reassigned.
questions.explanation: val makes the reference read-only, not the object behind it: a val holding a MutableList can still have items added. Prefer val by default; it makes code easier to follow and lets the compiler smart-cast more often.

questions.question: What does the compiler generate for a data class?
questions.answer: equals(), hashCode(), toString(), copy() and componentN() functions, all from the properties in the primary constructor.
questions.explanation: Only properties declared in the primary constructor take part, so a property declared in the class body is ignored by equals() and toString(). copy() returns a changed copy and componentN() makes destructuring work.
code: data class User(val name: String, val age: Int)

questions.question: When do you use lateinit instead of by lazy?
questions.answer: lateinit for a var that something else sets later, such as a framework or a test; by lazy for a val computed once on first access.
questions.explanation: lateinit works only on non-null var properties of non-primitive types, and reading one before it is assigned throws UninitializedPropertyAccessException. by lazy takes an initializer, runs it on first access and keeps the result; by default it is synchronized, so it is safe to read from several threads.
